 Player Stats

 LeBron James amassed 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics.
 James, who was inadvertently raked across the face by Paul George early in the fourth quarter, struggled against the Celtics. The good news for fantasy managers is that he committed just one turnover, but the 41-year-old shot the ball poorly. James, who entered Tuesday’s game shooting 25 percent from three, made just one of six three-point attempts. With the 76ers counting on Tyrese Maxey to be their lead scoring option, James’ ability to hit perimeter shots takes on added importance, and he’s struggling right now.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 LeBron James (sciatica) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Raptors. 
 James, who struggled in Tuesday’s loss to the Celtics, is back on the injury report to manage his sciatica. With Joel Embiid (foot) also questionable, the 76ers could be without two starters on Thursday. If LeBron sits, Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope should see their roles expand. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James accounted for 22 points (8-of-16 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Bulls. 
 After scoring eight points in a poor showing against the Cavaliers on Friday, James benefited from facing one of the NBA’s worst defenses on Sunday. The 41-year-old forward shot well and finished with his second game with at least 20 points, five rebounds and five assists this season. The 76ers play three games next week with no back-to-backs, which should help James get his rest. 
 Joel Embiid 
 PHI 
 Center-Forward 
 #21 
 Joel Embiid shot 0-of-9 from the field and 6-of-6 from the foul line in Friday’s loss to the Cavaliers, scoring six points with seven rebounds and one assist. 
 With Jarrett Allen (knee) out, many fantasy managers may have expected a big night from Embiid. He didn’t come through, to say the least. Embiid missed all nine of his shots from the field, with six free throws separating him from a scoreless night. The rebounds and blocks were decent, but this was a night to forget for Embiid and those rostering him. But he wasn’t alone, as LeBron James (8/7/3/2/1) shot 3-of-12 from the field and committed six turnovers. They’ll look to bounce back on Sunday against the Bulls.

 LeBron is back after missing Saturday’s win over the Hornets, the second game of a back-to-back. Who he pushes to the bench may depend on Joel Embiid (foot), who is questionable. If Embiid can play, Dean Wade would head to the bench. If Embiid can’t play, the 76ers could go without a true center, starting LeBron and Wade together, with Adem Bona on the bench.

 LeBron James (sciatica) is out for Saturday’s game against the Hornets. 
 James posted as 20/9/8 line in Friday’s win over the Knicks, but he’ll sit out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back. At age-41, LeBron isn’t going to play every night, but fantasy managers knew that going into the season. 
 LeBron James 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #23 
 LeBron James put up 20 points (8-of-15 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Knicks. 
 James made one of the game’s biggest plays, tipping in a Tyrese Maxey miss with 11.9 seconds remaining to extend the 76ers’ lead to five. That would be the final margin as Philadelphia moved to 5-1, and LeBron finished one rebound and two assists shy of a triple-double. At this stage in his career, the days of LeBron consistently providing robust stat lines are likely over. But he remains a valuable fantasy basketball player.

 LeBron James tallied 18 points (8-of-15 FGs, 2-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, five assists and two steals in Sunday’s loss to the Pistons. 
 Back in the lineup after sitting out Saturday’s win over the Bucks, James played 33 minutes on Sunday. Some of those minutes came at center, as the 76ers did not have Joel Embiid. James had a decent night, but he wasn’t as impactful as many fantasy managers likely hoped in the 76ers’ final game of Week 1.

 Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 The Thunder didn’t have Ajay Mitchell for Wednesday’s game, opening a spot in the starting lineup for Caruso. He took advantage of the opportunity, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. Caruso’s 14 points were a new season high for him, as he totaled 17 points in the first four games he played upon returning from an ankle injury. If Mitchell remains out for Friday’s game against the Clippers, Caruso would be worth rostering in 14-team leagues and some 12-team leagues.

 Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 After totaling 19 points in Oklahoma City’s first five games of November, Hartenstein recorded his first 20-point game of the season on Wednesday. The negative for iHart was the turnovers, of which he was responsible for six. A few of the turnovers were due to offensive fouls, so there isn’t much to worry about there. Rostered in 83 percent of Yahoo leagues, Hartenstein is providing top-100 fantasy value, slightly better than his ADP.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander produced 31 points (9-of-20 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 Gilgeous-Alexander has scored at least 30 points in six games this season. Unfortunately for him and the Thunder, the team’s lack of established scorers proved costly in both losses to the Trail Blazers. Five other Thunder players scored in double figures, with Isaiah Hartenstein’s 20 leading the way. The lack of creators who can take some of the pressure off of Gilgeous-Alexander was evident in both losses to the Trail Blazers. He’ll remain an elite fantasy option, but SGA’s ceiling may have taken a slight hit because a few of his teammates are injured.

 A double-digit scorer in seven straight games, Holiday provided solid fantasy value on Wednesday.  Sidy Cissoko produced 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
 Replacing Scoot Henderson (5/2/2 with one three-pointer) in the starting lineup ahead of Tuesday’s win over the Thunder, Cissoko played well in both victories. The Trail Blazers wing totaled 36 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Portland’s two-game sweep of Oklahoma City. While Cissoko isn’t a must-add player right now, he’s worth watching in deep leagues to see if the last two games were a fluke.

 Damian Lillard recorded 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
 While Lillard didn’t lead the way offensively for the Trail Blazers as he did in Wednesday’s win over Oklahoma City, the production remained solid. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of Portland’s first 11 games, and Dame has started every game. As long as he stays healthy, Lillard should be able to deliver a top-100 season, if not more.

 Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
 One night removed from scoring 24 points in a win over the Thunder, Avdija was just as productive in the rematch. The 28 points were the most he’s scored in a game since November 2, when the Trail Blazers forward hit that number in a win over the Nuggets. While there were questions before the season began about Portland’s offensive pecking order, there haven’t been any issues so far, even when the currently injured Ja Morant was healthy. That’s great for those who used a top-50 draft pick on Avdija.

 Melton’s final stat line wasn’t much to write home about, but his role may expand for Friday’s game against the Spurs. Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury and is expected to undergo an MRI on Thursday. If Curry misses time, Melton will have a larger role, whether he moves into the starting lineup or continues to come off the bench.
